These are existing business models we can bootstrap off of early. But what would it be like to extend that to every major industry?"

The AI buildout is running into a significant power constraint.

Greg Brockman on the next year at OpenAI and what he spends his time thinking about:

"The business is a huge area that we're not done yet with really up-leveling every part of execution. But I also think we are moving into a new phase of AI development."

"We call this the AGI era. And I think that that is something that you can debate. Is it this model, previous model, next model? It doesn't matter."

"It's objective. This is critical. It must happen. This is core to our mission."

"A lot of what I spend my time thinking about is making sure, do we have all the right processes? Are we talking about the right things? Do we have plans that really, at an operational level, at a practical level, lead us to... the kinds of safety guarantees that we view as core to our mission?"

"The theme of OpenAI, certainly for the past five years, has been deeper co-design, deeper intertwining across these functions that are maybe on the surface very disparate. All the way from go to market to long-term research to chip design."

"The areas that I will focus on will be dictated by the areas that most need that intertwining."

Everyone is asking "Where is Serenity" or "Who is Serenity". But nobody is asking...

"How is Serenity"?  

I do read things from $AMD $8.2B acquisition of World Labs... but feeling pretty sick right now, so taking a little break. 

I remember saying physical AI + world models would major shift way back when, so maybe I should have invested in private companies at the time... 

Apart from that... other interesting news:

- Some channel checks from ECOC was that $NVDA apparently secured 50% of $LITE Greensboro UHP laser capacity? And possibly contracts that allow them to secure the remaining capacity per Barclays. 

That's $5B in lasers (annual capacity)... so it's hilarious to see Nvidia go out and bottleneck the rest of the industry by doing this. But this just puts more strategic value on other merchant laser suppliers + more visibility for Lumentum.

It's kinda game theory over allocation, since if you secure all the HBM, lasers, and others it inadvertently makes it much harder for competitors to scale their programs. 

- Then there's your massive $150B Nvidia authorized buybacks (just look at $AAPL when they did buybacks..) They're printing too much. 

- What's also interesting is that Samsung Electro-Mechanics is expanding their FC-BGA substrate capacity today... but customers are the one funding this. 

I also remembered $MRVL in SEC filings cited large body substrates as one of the core bottlenecks of their program (alongside $TSM sole source dependencies). So they also went out and did some other expansion agreements with related companies like AT&S recently. 

- OpenAI delaying Astra-6.1 October release over safety concerns just now. Nvidia also happened to launch an AI safety platform. 

I don't think this is meaningfully bearish that the models are just getting 2 good.

tweets.text: To those who keep telling me that interest rates are just back to the long term normal, I agree but as it comes after 15 years of abnormal, therein lies the problem for those whose debt is coming due this year and next that was priced prior to 2022. The refi options are where the rate shock is. Just imagine the real estate operator who priced a 3% loan five years ago and is repricing at 8% this year, an ongoing adjustment seen over the past few years for those whose debt came due. We’ve of course seen the damage done to household mobility as many stick to their 3-4% mortgage rate and choose not to move. Or that SPAC and/or LBO in 2021 whose time has come to refi. Also, it is the rate of change and trajectory of the rate move that is the focus right now too, not only the absolute level.

Me, asking a machine that learned to think from me, whether machines can think. Strange loop, that.

But I wanted to test it properly. A more abstract philosophical question, to see if it reasons the way I would.

I asked it whether AI needs subjective experience to count as sentient... and it actually pushed back on the question entirely.

We cant measure subjective experience in humans either. We just assume other people have it because they look like us. So using it as the test for machines is trying to measure something unmeasurable.

What you can actually observe is reasoning, creativity... outputs that surprise the people who built them. Sapient by any practical measure. Whether they feel it, nobody knows. But feeling might not be the bar for mattering morally.

Not sure Id have answered it better.

4/ The attacker supplied an unusual offset of 0 for the transaction’s dynamic data. PaymentProcessor copied the data using the size of the entire call, shifting the victim’s address into the final 20 bytes and discarding the real caller's address. https://t.co/NDaxVo1FlT

6/ With `_msgSender()` forged, an attacker can make Payment Processor execute a trade as virtually any wallet with an outstanding approval.

The attacker created an offer for a victim’s NFT at no cost, they then made the contract believe the victim was accepting that offer. https://t.co/BzRXMsERGO

8/ At this point, I reached out to LimitBreak and simultaneously started looking for ways to brick PaymentProcessor.

7/ This is why cancelling listings would not have helped.

The attacker supplied the entire order. The only permission taken from the victim was their outstanding approval to Payment Processor.

7/ With the exploit already in the wild, we knew there was likely not much time before bigger drains began.

I set off to scan for assets at risk and began assembling a list. With hundreds of thousands of events to comb through, this unfortunately was a large, slow task.

6/ the LimitBreak team confirmed the finding and we started investigating ways to brick the contract. It could not be paused, so we looked at setting up reverting fee recipients, malformed forwarders, and anything else that could halt trading.

We found no way to shut it off.

9/ At this point, the cat was out of the bag and other wallets were exploiting. A helpful member from the osnipe discord stepped in and supplied supplementary lists from his own scans, an effort that was much appreciated, and resulted in many more saves throughout the night.

8/ We started executing batches of rescues around 1:46 AM EST, starting with the highest value assets. Working our way down the list. The scan continued in the background.

11/ At 4:45 AM I got pinged in discord again: a user had just been drained of WETH. I was still wrapping up my contract, and started pushing harder since I knew we likely only had minutes before all vulnerable WETH was gone.

10/ At 3:58 AM @0xjustadev realized that ERC20 balances may be at risk through a similar exploit path: 612 WETH and 8k USDC would be at risk if so.

I pivoted from the still-running NFT scan to look into ERC20s, and started building out a contract that could work to rescue them.

13/ At 5:06 AM, we had saved ~23,000 NFTs worth $5.9M USD. I posted a quick summary of the event, and climbed into bed to try to get some rest.

At 6:13 AM my 4 year old daughter woke me up, and when I looked at my phone I saw pings alerting me that more apes had been drained.

12/ At 4:53 my monitoring showed only 5 WETH left. I deployed and ran my unfinished contract as a hail mary which successfully drained the last ~3 available WETH but failed to transfer it to me. It is now stuck in that contract. 😭 https://t.co/jafGWk113o

14/ 18 apes. My scanner had caught them while I was building out the ERC20 contract, but I never circled back to it after losing the race to save WETH.

That will probably haunt me for the rest of my life.

16/ The community response has been overwhelming. People have given ETH, USDC, X Money, a bored ape from @AdamWeitsman, a meebit from @MeebitCompany, a 1:1 normie from @normiesART, brilliant commemorative art by @beeple @rolu_art @jackbutcher @boldleonidas, a hilarious video by @quirkiesnft, and more.

I appreciate all of you more than you know.

15/ That day, fueled entirely by rage and adrenaline, I built out https://t.co/SLbwhpBWJu: a self serve redistribution tool that allowed affected victims to reclaim what is rightfully theirs, powered by EIP7702 and merkle proofs.

17/ I am in contact with several parties involved in the exploit about return of funds. I will keep working around the clock to get as much as I can back in the hands of innocent victims.

19/ These donations enable me to devote a large amount of money on tokens to run intensive, persistent scans of important NFT infrastructure.

Attackers are doing it, and so we must do it too.

Our space is small and underrepresented, so it's up to us to make sure NFTs are safu.

18/ Malevolent parties will continue to attack our space. Education is our best defense. For that I recommend @BoringSecurity and all of its contributors (including myself).

Attackers will continue to get better.

It's important that defense does too.
